system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: Before each agent step, the system assembles a personalization contextCmem through two channels
system_prompt_style.note: Paper describes per-step assembly of RAG and memory context; the code that builds the system prompt was not in the evidence bundle (BaseAgent loads prompts via PromptManager).

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: The two candidate sets are fused via reciprocal rank fusion (Cormack et al., 2009), deduplicated, and truncated to a context budget, yielding the domain groundingCrag.
env_context_strategy.note: Embedding plus graph RAG over the knowledge base, combined with tool-driven investigation. Evidence is from the paper only.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: hierarchical compressionprogressively summarizes completed sub-goals into compact digests
context_compaction.note: Paper-only evidence. loop.py mentions a context-window guard, but its implementation was truncated from the bundle.

observation_format.evidence_quote: on the tool label, appends the assistant + tool messages and dispatches
observation_format.note: Tool-result format is inferred from the loop docstring; no conversion line was available.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: Native tool calling on every cloud OpenAI-compatible provider
tool_call_format.note: The loop also uses a first-line label protocol (THINK / tool label). DSML text tool calls are mentioned in the README; the parser was not in the evidence.

tool_count.note: The tool registry was not included in the evidence bundle.

edit_primitive.note: No edit tool definition was in the evidence. Co-Writer diffs are a user-facing UI feature, not an agent edit primitive.

tool_schema_source.note: The schema-producing code was not in the evidence. MCP servers are supported per the README.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: built-in tools, MCP servers, CLI apps

loop_primitives.evidence_quote:
The agentic loop drives a conversation with the LLM until one of the
caller-declared *terminal labels* fires.
loop_primitives.note: The default chat path is the react loop. Question generation uses validator-driven regeneration (paper Sec. 2.3). Deep Research is a multi-stage pipeline.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote:
it produces a tutoring planP=⟨𝑠 1,...,𝑠 𝐾⟩
of concrete, annotated sub-goals.
planning_granularity.note: Paper-only evidence. Mastery Path also stores a plan.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote:
A single agent loop
executes every capability
multi_agent_topology.note: Consultable subagents (consult_subagent) are reachable. Some capabilities use multiple specialised agents.

delegation_mechanism.note: Consults external agents (Claude Code, Codex) or Partners.

human_in_loop.note: No confirmation or permission code was in the evidence. The loop mentions pause handling, and book spine approval exists per the README.

short_term_state.evidence_quote:
self-notesdistill each step’s outcome
into a concise takeaway

long_term_memory.evidence_quote:
Every node
carries a dense embedding, enabling similarity-based retrieval across the entire forest.
long_term_memory.note: Evidence covers the trace forest (episodic, embedded), the learner profile, and installable skills. The file_notes value is inferred from the profile store.

state_persistence.note: The README mentions a restart-safe turn runtime, but no code was in the evidence.

self_verification.evidence_quote:
LLM-based verification assesses template alignment, factual correctness, and
pedagogical soundness for all items, while computational questions undergo additional sandboxed
code execution.

retry_policy.evidence_quote:
Failed pairs receive structured diagnostic
feedback and are regenerated until both pedagogical and factual constraints are met.

termination_condition.note: Terminal labels end the loop, which counts as model_declared.

cost_controls.note: Token tracking exists but no budget code was in the evidence.

execution_isolation.note: The README mentions a tool sandbox but gives no workspace code. Docker is a deployment option for the whole app.

permission_model.note: The README mentions deny-by-default MCP tools for non-admin users.

tracing.evidence_quote: L1 traces, L2 surface summaries, and L3 synthesis

replayability.evidence_quote: Partner conversations gain branch / resume / delete with a replayable trace

eval_hooks.note: TutorBench is described in the paper; whether its code is in the repo is unknown.

guardrails.note: The README mentions a skill install security gate.

target_domain.evidence_quote: DeepTutor is an agent-native learning workspace that connects tutoring, problem solving, quiz generation, research, visualization, and mastery practice in one extensible system.

primary_artifact.note: The repo postdates the paper (arXiv v3, Jul 2026).

first_release_date.note: First tag of the 1.x line per the README release list. Project first release was v0.2.0 (2026-01-02) or 2025-12-29.
